slides.title: 1. The Five Elements — Definitions at a Glance
slides.text:
1. The Five Elements — Definitions at a Glance
According to the IASB Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting, every financial statement item can be traced to one of five elements.
The Governing Equation
Assets = Liabilities + Equity
Assets, Liabilities, and Equity are balance sheet (position) elements — measured at a point in time. Income and Expenses are income statement (performance) elements — measured over a period. Net profit/Loss (Income − Expenses) flows into Retained Earnings, which is part of Equity — this is the thread that connects the two statements.
Element | Definition | Appears On
Assets | A present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past
events, with the potential to produce economic benefits. | Balance Sheet
Liabilities | A present obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result
of past events. | Balance Sheet
Equity | The residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities. | Balance Sheet
Income | Increases in assets, or decreases in liabilities, resulting in increases in equity
(other than owner contributions). Includes Revenues and Gains. | Income Statement
Expenses | Decreases in assets, or increases in liabilities, resulting in decreases in equity
(other than owner distributions). Includes Expenses and Losses. | Income Statement
